'''Robert Kurvitz''' (born 8 October 1984) is an Estonian [[novelist]], [[video game designer]], and musician. He was the lead writer and designer of the 2019 video game ''[[Disco Elysium]]'' as a founding member of the [[Disco Elysium#Development|ZA/UM]] cultural association and the eponymous [[video game development]] company that emerged from it. Kurvitz was fired from ZA/UM in 2022 after conflicts arose with investors who had acquired a majority stake in the company.<ref>{{cite web|title=TO FANS OF DISCO ELYSIUM, CONCERNING THE SITUATION AT ZA/UM|author1=Robert Kurvitz|author2=Aleksander Rostov|date=2022-11-10|url=https://medium.com/@artofrostov/to-fans-of-disco-elysium-concerning-the-situation-at-za-um-3e6bc46ea9c}}</ref>

==Life and career==

=== Early life ===
Kurvitz was born in Tallinn on 8 October 1984 to the artist couple [[Raoul Kurvitz]] and Lilian Mosolainen. By the age of fifteen, Kurvitz had dropped out of school.<ref name="bloody">{{Cite news |last=Bell |first=Alice |date=3 October 2019 |title=Disco Elysium's developers are in 'a bloody battle' for the human mind |work=Rock, Paper, Shotgun |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/disco-elysiums-developers-are-in-a-bloody-battle-for-the-human-mind |access-date=22 November 2021}}</ref> He became part of a group of peers called The Overcoats, a group of "5-10 high school dropouts...anarchists of some sort, with the motto: 'Today we drink tea, tomorrow we rule the world.'"

Long [[Pen-and-paper role-playing game|pen-and-paper role-playing]] sessions with this group were the beginning of the world that would become ''Disco Elysium''{{'}}s Elysium, and former Overcoats would form the core of the group that coalesced into the ZA/UM cultural association (not to be confused with ZA/UM Studio) in the late 2000s.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=ZA/UM |url=http://archive.org/details/discoelysiumartbook |title=Disco Elysium Digital Artbook |publisher=iam8bit |pages=}}</ref> The collective would later be described by ''[[The New York Times]]'' as a group of "leftist writers and artists who gathered in Tallinn".<ref name=NYT>{{cite web|title=A Group of Socialists Created a Hit Game That Tore Them Apart |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/09/17/arts/disco-elysium-zaum-estonia.html |date=17 September 2025 |access-date=14 June 2026 |author=Faber, Tom |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>

It was in this constellation that Kurvitz and some of the other artists began playing tabletop role-playing campaigns in a universe created and expanded over the years by Kurvitz himself. This universe called Elysium was characterized by [[steampunk]] elements, political turmoil and influenced by the participants' childhoods in the [[Eastern Bloc]]. It would be the setting of many ZA/UM projects, most notably Kurvitz 2013 novel ''Sacred and Terrible Air'' and the 2019 CRPG ''[[Disco Elysium]]''.<ref name=NYT/>

=== Music ===
In 2001, Kurvitz became the lyricist and lead singer of [[progressive rock]] band Ultramelanhool, which has seen by many as a continuation of the Estonian [[alternative rock]] tradition developed by [[Vennaskond]] and Metro Luminal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sõjaajaloolane Jüri Kot?inev vestab – üllatus, üllatus – täna hoopis muusikast. Ansamblist ultramelanhool. Ja sellest, miks eelmainit grupp tänases ja ehk ka homses kontekstis tähtis on |url=http://kes-kus.ee/sojaajaloolane-juri-kotinev-vestab-ullatus-ullatus-tana-hoopis-muusikast-ansamblist-ultramelanhool-ja-sellest-miks-eelmainit-grupp-tanases-ja-ehk-ka-homses-kontekstis-tahtis-on/ |website=KesKus |access-date=1 June 2016 |archive-date=7 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201107063746/http://kes-kus.ee/sojaajaloolane-juri-kotinev-vestab-ullatus-ullatus-tana-hoopis-muusikast-ansamblist-ultramelanhool-ja-sellest-miks-eelmainit-grupp-tanases-ja-ehk-ka-homses-kontekstis-tahtis-on/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=10 August 2004 |title=Ultramelanhool – päästerõngas uppunule? |url=https://www.postimees.ee/1427481/ultramelanhool-paasterongas-uppunule |website=Postimees}}</ref> The literary scientist Jaak Tomberg argued, however, that such easy comparisons may do a disservice to the band's actual original character.<ref>{{Cite web |last=OKIA |title=Kui bänd astub lavale |url=https://sirp.ee/s1-artiklid/c5-muusika/kui-b-nd-astub-lavale/ |access-date=2021-11-29 |website=Sirp |language=et}}</ref> To date, they have released two albums, {{lang|et|italic=yes|Must apelsin}} (''Black Orange'') and {{lang|et|italic=yes|Materjal}} (''Material''), in 2004 and 2008 respectively.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eesti rahvusbibliograafia |url=https://erb.nlib.ee/?komp=&otsi=Ultramelanhool+(ansambel),+esitaja+(album)&register=autorid&r_oid=c97b7a35 |website=erb.nlib.ee}}</ref>

The band failed to secure an Estonian record label for their second album. It was then self-released with money inherited by Kurvitz's long-time friend, editor, and collaborator Martin Luiga, and released on the internet for free.<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 September 2008 |title=Hüvasti plaadid, tere veebimuusika! |url=https://www.postimees.ee/34503/huvasti-plaadid-tere-veebimuusika |website=Postimees}}</ref> In 2011, Kurvitz collaborated on his father Raoul's album ''Forbidden to Sing'', providing backing vocals and keyboards.<ref>{{Cite web |year=2011 |title=Eesti rahvusbibliograafia |url=https://erb.nlib.ee/?kid=27199587 |website=erb.nlib.ee}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Raoul Kurvitz |url=https://noar.eu/et/kunstnik/raoul-kurvitz/ |website=NOAR}}</ref>

=== Literature ===
In 2013, Kurvitz published the novel ''Sacred and Terrible Air'' ({{langx|et|Püha ja õudne lõhn}}), on which he had worked over five years.<ref>{{Cite web |first=Johanna |last=Ross |date=2014-06-11|title=Värske Rõhk: Kirjanduse võidurelvastumine. Intervjuu Robert Kurvitzaga|trans-title=Fresh Emphasis: The triumph of literature. Interview with Robert Kurvitz |url=https://kultuur.err.ee/299678/varske-rohk-kirjanduse-voidurelvastumine-intervjuu-robert-kurvitzaga |access-date=2021-11-22 |website=ERR |language=et}}</ref> The novel, set in the fictional world of Elysium, centers on three men who, twenty years after the unexplained disappearance of their classmates, are still determined to locate them. It received positive reviews,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.delfi.ee/a/67229810 |title=Nädala raamat: Kurvitza püha ja õudne aegruum |trans-title=Book of the Week: The Sacred and Terrible Spacetime of Kurvitza |date=30 November 2013 |website=Eesti Ekspress}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.digar.ee/viewer/et/nlib-digar:195251/143104/page/158|title=Vikerkaar; 4–5 2014-05 |website=Digar}}</ref>{{failed verification|reason=There's nothing here!|date=February 2022}} with literary theorist Johanna Ross highlighting it as one of the few books to successfully bridge science fiction and "literature proper".<ref name="va">{{cite web |url=http://va.ee/10-sisukord/63-kirjanduse-voidurelvastumine-intervjuu-robert-kurvitzaga |title=Kirjanduse võidurelvastumine. Intervjuu Robert Kurvitzaga |website=va.ee |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140811145149/http://va.ee/10-sisukord/63-kirjanduse-voidurelvastumine-intervjuu-robert-kurvitzaga |archive-date=2014-08-11}}</ref>

Literary scientist Jaak Tomberg emphasized the great attention to detail in his review: "Through that novel we bear witness to (1) a style which seems to be in its actually realistic and simply reflective way to be attentive towards the world to an almost paranoid degree, and (2) to a made-up world, which in its relentless interconnectedness is far more systemic than the reality we recognize as 'our own' and also remarkably more systemic than most of the fictional ones, which may by their similar way of building reservedly be called 'fantastic'."<ref>{{Cite web|last=ERR|first=Jaak Tomberg |date=2014-01-11|title=Sirp, Jaak Tomberg Robert Kurvitza romaanist|url=https://kultuur.err.ee/296101/sirp-jaak-tomberg-robert-kurvitza-romaanist|access-date=2021-12-05|website=ERR|language=et}}</ref> Despite its positive critical reception, the book was a commercial failure, selling between 1,000 and 1,500 copies, and causing Kurvitz to "succumb to a deep alcoholism".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/the-making-of-disco-elysium-how-zaum-created-one-of-the-most-original-rpgs-of-the-decade/ |title=The making of Disco Elysium: How ZA/UM created one of the most original RPGs of the decade |first=Alex |last=Wiltshire |date=9 January 2020 |access-date=8 April 2020 |work=[[GamesRadar]]}}</ref> An English translation was planned for 2020, but it did not occur. As of 2023, two English fan translations exist.<ref>{{Cite web|title=I caught ''Disco Elysium'' fever. No, not the Saturday Night kind. I was really quite poorly |url=https://www.theregister.com/2019/12/27/disco_elysium/ |access-date=27 February 2022 |date=27 December 2019 |last=Currie |first=Richard |website=The Register}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Why the Creator of Disco Elysium Hasn't Read the Reviews, and What's Next for the IP |url=https://www.escapistmagazine.com/why-the-creator-of-disco-elysium-hasnt-read-the-reviews-and-whats-next-for-the-ip/ |first=Samantha |last=Nelson |date=1 November 2019 |access-date=10 April 2023 |work=The Escapist |quote="[Kurvitz is] also focused on an English translation of ''Sacred and Terrible Air'' that will be released next year, but has not yet been published"}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Disco Elysium novel Sacred and Terrible Air has finally been translated |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/disco-elysium-novel-sacred-and-terrible-air-has-finally-been-translated/ |first=Jody|last=Macgregor|date=12 May 2023 |access-date=15 May 2023 |work=PC Gamer |quote="Fortunately, the videogame was a little more successful, which resulted in plans to translate it into English. However, the announced 2020 release window passed without comment."}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Thanks to fans, Sacred and Terrible Air, a novel set in the same world as Disco Elysium, finally has its English translation|author=Anne-Marie Ostler|date=2023-05-12|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/thanks-to-fans-sacred-and-terrible-air-a-novel-set-in-the-same-world-as-disco-elysium-finally-has-its-english-translation/|website=[[GamesRadar]]}}</ref>

Having played [[tabletop roleplaying games]] for much of his life, Kurvitz uses [[worldbuilding]] techniques derived from ''[[Dungeons & Dragons]]'', though opting for a pseudo-modernist fantasy world instead of a pseudo-medieval one. He employs help in the development of his ideas. "Mass editing" was employed as a tool in the finishing stage of the book; people of varying backgrounds assessed the readability and realism of the work, pointing out confusing passages and suggesting amendments.<ref name="va" />

=== Video games ===
After years of leading tabletop campaigns and expanding their own setting, the world of Elysium, the idea was brought up to develop a game set in this world. In 2015 Kurvitz started to recruit members of the ZA/UM cultural association and the following year he founded the [[video game development]] company ZA/UM.<ref name=NYT/> After a five year development cycle the [[Single-player video game|single-player]] [[computer roleplaying game]] titled ''[[Disco Elysium]]'', was released on 15 October 2019. Kurvitz was the game's lead writer and designer,<ref>{{cite web |last=Marzano |first=Anthony |date=15 October 2019 |title=Police procedural cRPG ''Disco Elysium'' is out today |url=https://www.destructoid.com/police-procedural-crpg-disco-elysium-is-out-today-569627.phtml |access-date=16 October 2019 |publisher=[[Destructoid]]}}</ref><ref name="Gamesindustry">{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Haydn |date=31 October 2018 |title=Chasing oblivion with ''Disco Elysium'' and alcohol addiction |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2018-10-31-disco-elysium |website=Gamesindustry.biz}}</ref><ref name="Kurvitz">{{cite magazine |last1=Macgregor |first1=Jody |date=2 November 2019 |title=Disco Elysium's lead designer wants to make an expansion and sequel, has already written a novel |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/disco-elysiums-lead-designer-wants-to-make-an-expansion-and-sequel-has-already-written-a-novel/ |magazine=PC Gamer |access-date=13 November 2019}}</ref> having produced about half of the total in-game text (half a million words).<ref name="bloody" /> It received universal acclaim, being named as a [[List of Game of the Year awards|game of the year]] by several publications, along with numerous other awards for its narrative and art.<ref name="TGA2019">{{cite web |last=Makuch |first=Eddie |date=13 December 2019 |title=The Game Awards 2019 Winners: Sekiro Takes Game Of The Year |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/the-game-awards-2019-winners-sekiro-takes-game-of-/1100-6472169/ |access-date=13 December 2019 |website=GameSpot}}</ref><ref name="WashingtonPost">{{cite news |last=Byrd |first=Christopher |date=17 October 2019 |title='Disco Elysium': Riveting delirium |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/video-games/reviews/disco-elysium-riveting-delirium/ |access-date=18 October 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=9 December 2019 |title=The 25 Best Video Games of 2019 |url=https://www.slantmagazine.com/features/the-25-best-video-games-of-2019/5/ |access-date=15 December 2019 |website=Slant}}</ref>

Kurvitz claims to have developed the Elysium world since he was fifteen or sixteen, originally inspired by "a bootleg Finnish Middle Earth roleplay system". The game is also notable for having far less emphasis on violence than the norm for the RPG genre.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 September 2021 |title=Tabletop Fest - Disco Elysium - A chat with Robert Kurvitz, lead writer and designer |url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/group/38511516/view/3989616160691586364 |access-date=22 November 2021 |work=Steam News}}</ref> Kurvitz considers some aspects of ''Disco Elysium'' "essentially [[Soviet Union|Soviet]]", referencing the Soviet Union's [[Soviet science fiction|tradition]] of [[science fiction literature]] and the works of the [[Arkady and Boris Strugatsky|Strugatsky brothers]] in particular. "They were people who took responsibility for the [[heat death of the universe]]. When they were writing books, this needed to contribute to the [[ultimate fate of the universe]]. Because they didn't have money obligations, so what are your obligations then? So this kind of serious responsibility for, what the fuck does a piece of entertainment really do to the human mind, and what are the responsibilities therein, that I think is very, very, very prevalent in ''Disco Elysium''."<ref name="bloody"/>

''Disco Elysium: The Final Cut'', an expanded version of the game, was released in 2021 and work on its sequel, code-named 'Y12', was underway at this point, as was reported later, but was cut short by the involuntary departure of Kurvitz, art director Aleksander Rostov and ''Final Cut'' lead writer Helen Hindpere from ZA/UM. The project was eventually shelved by the company, following a lack of direction without many of the original game's senior developers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/gaming-industry/game-development/for-a-while-it-seemed-like-miracles-were-possible-and-with-them-redemption-a-follow-up-to-the-legendary-disco-elysium-might-have-been-ready-to-play-within-the-next-yearzaums-devs-loved-it-management-canceled-it-and-laid-off-the-team/ |title=A follow-up to the legendary Disco Elysium might have been ready to play within the next year⁠—ZA/UM's devs loved it, management canceled it and laid off the team: 'For a while it seemed like miracles were possible, and with them redemption' |author=Litchfield, Ted |date=13 June 2024 |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref>

==== Red Info ====
In 2025 it was reported by the ''[[Financial Times]]'' that Kurvitz, Rostov and Hindpere have founded another game studio called Red Info where they are working on a new project together with American game developer [[Chris Avellone]], who was the lead writer on 1999's ''[[Planescape: Torment]]'', a central influence on ''Disco Elysium''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/5ae5bf4f-4c05-4286-8133-5b812309d636 |title=The curse of 'Disco Elysium', the greatest RPG ever made |website=[[Financial Times]] |date=2 August 2025 |access-date=14 June 2026 |author=Fyfe, Duncan}}</ref> They have secured a $10 million investment by the Chinese tech company [[NetEase]].<ref name=NYT/>

=== Politics ===
A [[Communism|communist]], Kurvitz has a green-gold bust of Russian revolutionary [[Vladimir Lenin]] on his writing desk, which he claimed formerly belonged to Estonian Soviet writer [[Juhan Smuul]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Ambria |title=The Disco Elysium Saga Shows Why Creative Workers Need to Band Together |url=https://jacobin.com/2023/09/disco-elysium-intellectual-property-video-game-industry-creative-workers-collective-action |access-date=2024-12-24 |website=Jacobin |language=en-US |quote=I would have thought my spiritual history as an absolute rancid communist might help me in this situation a little bit. But no, no one wants this kind of fight, and it didn’t prepare me in any way for this stuff.}}</ref> "I guess my favourite thing I like to say about this is that for me it's just a wholesome tradition. It's about loyalty, it's about the country where I was born. This is how I was raised, this was who I was told to follow, and I would be a naughty revolutionary, kind of an edgy rebel, if I wouldn't have Lenin on my writing desk."<ref name="bloody"/> Kurvitz is a follower of [[Hegelian dialectics]], which he describes as "the central principle of Elysium's worldbuilding." Dialectics and other leftist historical theories were essential for Elysium's development, forming the basis for critical elements of the world's history, such as the innocentic system.<ref name=":1" />

== Legal issues and controversies ==

=== 2013 ''Sirp'' controversy ===
In November 2013, [[Kaur Kender]], Kurvitz's longtime friend and collaborator on ''A Sacred and Terrible Air'', was announced as editor-in-chief of the Estonian cultural magazine ''[[Sirp]]''. Kender soon brought Kurvitz on as an editor. Kender's appointment was criticized by many in the press and some artists for their "undemocratic" nature on the part of the Ministry of Culture, though these protests were also criticized for exaggerating the problem.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Valme |first=Valner |date=2013-11-25 |title=Grünberg: Kender tõi särtsu |url=https://kultuur.err.ee/295193/grunberg-kender-toi-sartsu |access-date=2023-10-29 |website=ERR |language=et}}</ref>

Less than a month later, both Kender and Kurvitz announced their resignations from the magazine after they published an unpublished work by poet Andres Aule, which was done without his consent. In their statement, they said that they had made "a grave mistake" and "[did] not see the possibility of continuing."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lust |first=Katrin |date=25 November 2013 |title=Kaur Kender ja Robert Kurvitz panid pillid kotti |url=https://elu24.postimees.ee/2608576/kaur-kender-ja-robert-kurvitz-panid-pillid-kotti |access-date=29 October 2023 |website=Postimees |language=et}}</ref> In the ''Disco Elysium'' official artbook, Kurvitz described the situation as "a suicidal manoeuvre that constituted the pathetic crescendo of our national careers, an unremovable stain, an unforgivable sin."<ref name=":1" />

=== Removal from ZA/UM ===
In October 2022, Kurvitz, along with art director Aleksander Rostov and writer Helen Hindpere of ZA/UM, were announced by member Martin Luiga in a [[Medium (website)|Medium]] post to have, along with Luiga himself, "involuntarily left the company", stating that ZA/UM "no longer represents the ethos it was founded on." Luiga also revealed that the original ZA/UM [[Cultural institution|cultural association]] had been dissolved.<ref name="pcgamer departures">{{Cite web |last=Litchfield |first=Ted |date=1 October 2022 |title=Founding member of Disco Elysium developer claims core team members 'involuntarily' left the company |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/founding-member-of-disco-elysium-developer-claims-core-team-members-involuntarily-left-the-company/ |access-date=1 October 2022 |website=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref> In an interview, Luiga stated that Kurvitz and the other members had been fired under [[false premise]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Laska |first=Karol |date=6 October 2022 |title='Fans Have the Right to Know' - Disco Elysium Co-Creator Talks ZA/UM Losing With the System |url=https://www.gamepressure.com/newsroom/fans-have-the-right-to-know-disco-elysium-co-creator-talks-zaum-l/z04ad7 |access-date=6 October 2022 |website=Gamepressure.com |language=en}}</ref> A ZA/UM spokesperson stated to ''[[Eurogamer]]'' that "Like any video game, the development of ''Disco Elysium'' was and still is a collective effort, with every team member's contribution essential and valued as part of a greater whole. At this time, we have no further comment to make other than the ZA/UM creative team's focus remains on the development of our next project, and we are excited to share more news on this with you all soon."<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Batchelor |first=James |date=3 October 2022 |title=Three key members of Disco Elysium studio have left 'involuntarily' |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/three-key-members-of-disco-elysium-studio-have-left-involuntarily |magazine=[[Game Informer]] |access-date=8 October 2022}}</ref>

Additional statements were released by the conflicting parties in early November 2022. Kurvitz and Rostov together claimed that Zaum Studio OÜ, the development studio, was originally owned in majority shares by Margus Linnamäe and was then acquired by Tütreke OÜ, a holding company owned by studio CEO Ilmar Kompus through a share purchase in 2021. Kurvitz and Rostov claimed that the funds used for that purchase were pulled from the studio itself, making it a fraudulent purchase; on this basis they sought to challenge the purchase and recover their IP from the studio.<ref name="gr nov2022">{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Dustin |date=November 9, 2022 |title=Fired Disco Elysium devs allege fraud, while the studio alleges toxic management |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/fired-disco-elysium-devs-allege-fraud-while-the-studio-alleges-toxic-management/ |access-date=November 9, 2022 |website=[[GamesRadar]]}}</ref> The pair alleged that Kompus purchased four sketches from Zaum that were establishing the basis for a ''Disco Elysium'' sequel for {{GBP|1}}, then resold these to Zaum for {{Euro|4.8 million}}, effectively helping Kompus regain part of the money spent to acquire Zaum through Tütreke.

Kurvitz and Rostov discovered the change in how the company was organized, including their demotion, and alleged that they were fired when they began asking questions. Kurvitz and Rostov argued that they still have some control of the ''Disco Elysium'' [[intellectual property]] rights, and thus should have had a say in blocking the sale.<ref name="gr nov2022" /><ref name="pcgamer legal update">{{Cite web |last=Straton |first=Rich |date=November 22, 2022 |title=The legal war over Disco Elysium reaches Disco Elysium levels of complexity |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/the-legal-war-over-disco-elysium-reaches-disco-elysium-levels-of-complexity/ |access-date=November 24, 2022 |website=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref> Zaum Studio released a statement dismissing the charges, saying that the former employees had been let go for creating a disruptive environment at the studio, that the two had "limited to no engagement in their responsibility and work", and that they had verbally abused and engaged in gender discrimination against other employees.<ref name="pcgamer legal update" />

Other employees of Zaum Studio speaking anonymously with ''[[GamesIndustry.biz]]'' claimed the situation lay between these points.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Partis |first=Danielle |date=November 9, 2022 |title=Disco Elysium studio ZA/UM confirms former employees were fired for misconduct |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/disco-elysium-studio-zaum-confirms-former-employees-were-fired-for-misconduct |access-date=November 9, 2022 |website=[[GamesIndustry.biz]]}}</ref> A later investigation by ''[[People Make Games]]'' corroborated some of the studio's accusations, with Kurvitz in particular singled out by some other employees, who assumed lead roles subsequent to his ousting, for poor management and creating a hostile work environment, especially during ''Disco Elysium''{{'}}s long period of [[Crunch (video games)|crunch]].<ref name=":0">{{Citation |title=Investigation: Who's Telling the Truth about Disco Elysium? |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JGIGA8taN-M |access-date=2023-05-30 |language=en}}</ref>

Legal proceedings in the matter were started by Kaur Kender, the executive producer of ''Disco Elysium'' and Kurvitz's longtime friend and collaborator. An initial hearing in Kender's case, which included statements from Kurvitz, was held in October 2022.<ref name="pcgamer legal update" /> By December 2022, Kender had dropped his lawsuit, as Kompus had paid back {{Euro|4.8 million}} from Tütreke back to ZA/UM.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Partis |first=Danielle |date=December 8, 2022 |title=Lawsuit against ZA/UM majority shareholder withdrawn |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/lawsuit-against-zaum-majority-shareholder-withdrawn |access-date=December 8, 2022 |website=[[GamesIndustry.biz]]}}</ref><ref name="pcgamer dec2022">{{Cite web |last=Litchfield |first=Ted |date=December 10, 2022 |title=$4.8 million paid to ZA/UM and one lawsuit dropped as the battle over Disco Elysium continues |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/dollar48-million-paid-to-zaum-and-one-lawsuit-dropped-as-the-battle-over-disco-elysium-continues/ |access-date=December 10, 2022 |website=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref> Kurvitz and Rostov still assert that there were illegal actions to take over the development studio leading to their ouster.<ref name="pcgamer dec2022" />

The studio issued a statement on 14 March 2023 stating that all legal actions from the former members were concluded. The studio alleged that Kurvitz and Rostov's lawsuit was dropped due to a lack of evidence. Further details of these cases remain confidential.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wales |first=Matt |date=March 14, 2023 |title=Disco Elysium studio says lawsuits from former members have been resolved |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/disco-elysium-studio-says-lawsuits-from-former-members-have-been-resolved |access-date=March 14, 2023 |website=[[Eurogamer]]}}</ref> However, on 17 March 2023, Kurvitz and another former ZA/UM creative, Sander Taal (the real legal name of Rostov, according to ZA/UM<ref>{{Cite web |last=Partis |first=Danielle |date=2022-11-09 |title=Disco Elysium studio ZA/UM confirms former employees were fired for misconduct |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/disco-elysium-studio-zaum-confirms-former-employees-were-fired-for-misconduct |access-date=2023-10-30 |website=GamesIndustry.biz |language=en}}</ref>), responded to this statement by clarifying that the announcement was "wrong and misleading in several respects" and "[sought] to unfairly paint [them] - the remaining minority shareholders in ZA/UM - as mere disgruntled employees." Kurvitz and Taal also stated that their lawsuit regarding employment claims against the studio was dismissed "as part of a larger campaign against [them]" and that they plan to "pursue legal options accordingly." This statement additionally makes clear a rift between Kurvitz and his longtime collaborator Kender, stating "Unlike Kender, we [Kurvitz and Taal] have not participated in the looting of ZA/UM".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Litchfield |first=Ted |date=March 18, 2023 |title=Disco Elysium studio declares 'resolution' of legal battle while two of its ousted founders insist the fight continues: 'they will not silence us' |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/disco-elysium-studio-declares-resolution-of-legal-battle-while-two-of-its-ousted-founders-insist-the-fight-continues-they-will-not-silence-us/ |access-date=March 19, 2023 |website=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rousseau |first=Jeffrey |date=2023-03-14 |title=ZA/UM resolves legal dispute with Disco Elysium producer Kaur Kender |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/zaum-resolves-legal-dispute-with-disco-elysium-producer-kaur-kender |access-date=2023-03-21 |website=[[GamesIndustry.biz]] |language=en}}</ref>
